facts.statement: Ouranosaurus measured approximately 7 to 8.3 meters in length and weighed about 2.2 tonnes.
facts.quote: Ouranosaurus measured about 7 - 8.3 m long and weighed 2.2 MT.

facts.statement: Two nearly complete fossils of Ouranosaurus were discovered in the Elrhaz Formation in Agadez, Niger, in 1965 and 1970.
facts.quote: Two rather complete fossils were found in the Elrhaz Formation, Gadoufaoua deposits, Agadez, Niger, in 1965 and 1970

facts.statement: The genus Ouranosaurus was named in 1976 by the French paleontologist Philippe Taquet.
facts.quote: The animal was named in 1976 by French paleontologist Philippe Taquet

facts.statement: The generic name Ouranosaurus combines the word 'ourane' with the Greek word 'sauros' meaning lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name is a combination of ourane, a word with multiple meanings, and sauros, the Greek word for lizard.

facts.statement: The specific epithet nigeriensis refers to Niger, the country where the fossils were discovered.
facts.quote: The specific epithet nigeriensis alludes to Niger, its country of discovery

facts.statement: Five French expeditions led by Philippe Taquet explored the Gadoufaoua region of the Sahara Desert in Niger between 1965 and 1972.
facts.quote: Five French palaeontological expeditions were undertaken in the Gadoufaoua region of the Sahara Desert in Niger between 1965 and 1972 and led by French palaeontologist Philippe Taquet.

facts.statement: The first expedition in January–February 1965 discovered eight iguanodontian specimens at the "niveau des Innocents" site.
facts.quote: On the first expedition, lasting from January–February 1965, eight iguanodontian specimens were discovered at the "niveau des Innocents" site

facts.statement: Two additional skeletons were found 7 km southeast of Elrhaz at the "Camp des deux Arbres" locality.
facts.quote: An additional two skeletons were discovered 7 km southeast of Elrhaz in the "Camp des deux Arbres" locality

facts.statement: Philippe Taquet formally described specimens MNHN GDF 300 and MNHN GDF 381 as Ouranosaurus nigeriensis in 1976.
facts.quote: Taquet formally described the two mostly-complete specimens MNHN GDF 300 and MNHN GDF 381 from the first and fourth expeditions as Ouranosaurus nigeriensis in 1976

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MNHN GDF 300 included a semi-articulated skull missing the left maxilla and right quadratojugal, almost the entire vertebral column, and most of the right hindlimb.
facts.quote: MNHN GDF 300 was made the holotype, and was the primary specimen described, including a semi-articulated skull lacking the left maxilla, right quadratojugal and the articulars, almost the entire vertebral column, forelimbs lacking a few hand bones, and most of the right hindlimb and a few bones of the left.

facts.statement: The holotype was returned to Niger and is now displayed at the Musée National Boubou Hama in Niamey.
facts.quote: The holotype itself was returned to Niger after being described and having its bones cast and mounted, and is now on display at the Musée National Boubou Hama in Niamey.

facts.statement: The name Ouranosaurus has a double meaning derived from Arabic words for bravery and the Tuareg name for the desert monitor lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name Ouranosaurus carries a double meaning, it is both taken from Arabic meaning "valour", "bravery" or "recklessness" and also from the local Tuareg language of Niger where it is the name they call the desert monitor.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested in 2017 that the holotype and paratype specimens were subadults but close to adult size.
facts.quote: The holotype and paratype specimens were suggested to belong to subadults by Bertozzo et al. in 2017, although they would have been close to adult size.

facts.statement: The size variation between specimens fits within the range seen in adult Iguanodon, suggesting they may have been in the same ontogenetic stage.
facts.quote: The variation between the sizes fits within the range of variation between adult individuals of Iguanodon, so there is a chance that the larger holotype and smaller paratype were in the same ontogenetic stage.

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus had a skull that was 67.0 centimeters long.
facts.quote: The skull of Ouranosaurus is 67.0 cm long.

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus possessed the most elongated skull of any non-hadrosaurid dinosaur, with a length 3.8 times its maximum height.
facts.quote: This makes Ouranosaurus have the most elongate skull of any non-hadrosaurid, the length being 3.8 times the maximum height

facts.statement: The premaxillae bones of Ouranosaurus were 46.0 centimeters long and featured very deep external nostrils.
facts.quote: The premaxillae are 46.0 cm long, with very deep external nares

facts.statement: The known right maxilla of Ouranosaurus formed a triangle measuring 28.0 centimeters in length and 11.7 centimeters in height.
facts.quote: Only the right maxilla of Ouranosaurus is known, although it is well preserved forming a triangle 28.0 cm long and 11.7 cm tall

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus had a toothless snout covered in a horny sheath that formed a wide beak, matching a similar sheath on the lower jaw's predentary bone.
facts.quote: The snout was toothless and covered in a horny sheath during life, forming a very wide beak together with a comparable sheath on the short predentary bone at the extreme front of the lower jaws.

facts.statement: A large sail supported by long, wide neural spines spanning the entire rump and tail was the most conspicuous feature of Ouranosaurus.
facts.quote: The most conspicuous feature of Ouranosaurus is a large "sail" on its back, supported by long, wide, neural spines, that spanned its entire rump and tail.

facts.statement: The tenth, eleventh, and twelfth neural spines of Ouranosaurus were the longest, reaching about 63 centimeters.
facts.quote: The tenth, eleventh and twelfth spines are the longest, at about 63 cm.

facts.statement: The humerus of Ouranosaurus was very straight and large, measuring 555 millimeters in length.
facts.quote: The humerus was very straight and large, measuring 555 mm in proximodistal (top bottom) length.

facts.statement: The foot of Ouranosaurus was narrow, featuring only three relatively long toes.
facts.quote: The foot was narrow with only three toes and relatively long.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the back of Ouranosaurus carried a sail or a hump of muscle tissue or fat similar to a bison or camel.
facts.quote: An alternative hypothesis is that the back might have carried a hump consisting of muscle tissue or fat, resembling that of a bison or camel, rather than a sail.

facts.statement: The leg structure of Ouranosaurus suggests the legs were used as pillars for support rather than for sprinting.
facts.quote: This may indicate that the legs were used as pillars, and not for sprinting.

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus was originally assigned to the family Iguanodontidae in 1976, but this family is now considered paraphyletic and is no longer used.
facts.quote: Ouranosaurus was assigned to the family Iguanodontidae in 1976, though this family is now considered paraphyletic within Iguanodontia and is no longer used.

facts.statement: A 2011 study by McDonald and colleagues classified Ouranosaurus as a basal member of the clade Hadrosauriformes.
facts.quote: McDonald and colleagues (2011) found Ouranosaurus to be a basal member of Hadrosauriformes, the clade containing Hadrosauroidea and several basal hadrosauriformes.

facts.statement: A 2025 analysis by Lockwood and colleagues recovered Ouranosaurus as the sister taxon to a group within Styracosterna, diverging just before Hadrosauriformes.
facts.quote: In the 2025 description of the British styracosternan Istiorachis by Lockwood and colleagues, their phylogenetic analysis recovered Ouranosaurus as the sister taxon to the taxon within the ankylopollexian clade Styracosterna, diverging immediately before the Hadrosauriformes.

facts.statement: The species Ouranosaurus nigeriensis was described by Taquet in 1976.
facts.quote: species_authority: Taquet, 1976

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 110 million years ago in the Aptian stage, in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 110 millones de años durante el Aptiense, en lo que hoy es África.

facts.statement: The fossils were found in 1966 in the Echkar or El Rhaz Formation at Gadoufaoua, Agadez, Niger, and the genus was named in 1976 by French paleontologist Philippe Taquet.
facts.quote: Encontrado en la Formación Echkar o El Rhaz, en los depósitos de Gadoufaouna, Agadez, Níger, en 1966 y fue nombrado en 1976 por el paleontólogo francés Philippe Taquet.

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus was a herbivore that walked on two legs but could also walk on four, measuring about 7 meters in length and weighing 4 tonnes.
facts.quote: Ouranosaurus era un herbívoro, bípedo y facultativamente cuadrúpedo que medía unos 7 metros de longitud, y un peso de 4 toneladas.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul suggested in 2010 that Ouranosaurus weighed only 2.2 tonnes but could reach a length of 8.3 meters.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul sugirió un peso más ligero de 2,2 toneladas en 2010 aunque se le dio una longitud mayor de 8,3 metros.

facts.statement: Specimen MSNVE 3714 is mounted at 6.5 meters long, representing about 90% of the holotype's estimated length of 7.22 meters.
facts.quote: MSNVE 3714 tiene 6,5 metros de largo tal como está montado, aunque faltan algunas caudales, y tiene aproximadamente el 90% de la longitud del holotipo, que tendría 7,22 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus had jaws operated by relatively weak muscles.
facts.quote: The jaws were apparently operated by relatively weak muscles.

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus likely used its teeth to chew tough plant food.
facts.quote: Ouranosaurus probably used its teeth to chew up tough plant food.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest a diet of leaves, fruit, and seeds, while the wide beak indicates specialization for eating large amounts of low-quality fodder.
facts.quote: A diet has been suggested of leaves, fruit, and seeds as the chewing would allow to free more energy from high quality food; the wide beak on the other hand indicates a specialisation in eating large amounts of low quality fodder.

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus is known from the Elrhaz Formation of the Tegama Group in the Gadoufaoua area of Niger.
facts.quote: Ouranosaurus is known from the Elrhaz Formation of the Tegama Group in an area called Gadoufaoua, located in Niger.

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus lived in the upper portion of the Elrhaz Formation, which is probably Aptian in age.
facts.quote: Ouranosaurus is from the upper portion of the formation, probably Aptian in age.

facts.statement: Evidence of remodeling and high vascular density in the subadult paratype suggests that Ouranosaurus experienced fast growth.
facts.quote: Remodeling is present in the subadult paratype, and high vascular density and circumferential arrangement of the microstructure suggests fast growth.

facts.statement: The phylogenetic relationships of Ouranosaurus remained uncertain for decades after its description.
facts.quote: The relationships of Ouranosaurus were uncertain for decades following its description.

facts.statement: While Lurdusaurus and Nigersaurus were the most numerous megaherbivores in the Elrhaz Formation, Ouranosaurus was also a dominant element of the ecosystem.
facts.quote: The iguanodontian Lurdusaurus and the rebbachisaurid Nigersaurus were the most numerous megaherbivores in the Elrhaz formation, although Ouranosaurus was a dominant element as well.

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus lived alongside the theropods Kryptops, Suchomimus, Eocarcharia, and Afromimus.
facts.quote: It also lived alongside the theropods Kryptops, Suchomimus, Eocarcharia, and Afromimus.

facts.statement: The skull of Ouranosaurus measured 67.0 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Ouranosaurus mide 67,0 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: The skull was quite low, measuring 24.4 centimeters wide and only 26.0 centimeters high.
facts.quote: Era bastante bajo, con 24,4 centímetros de ancho y solo 26,0 centímetros de alto.

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus possesses the most elongated skull of all non-hadrosaurids, with a length 3.8 times its maximum height.
facts.quote: Esto hace que Ouranosaurus tenga el cráneo más alargado de todos los no hadrosáuridos, la longitud es 3.8 veces la altura máxima

facts.statement: The jaws lacked teeth in the front portion but featured a large flat beak larger than that of Iguanodon.
facts.quote: No presentaba dientes en la porción frontal de sus mandíbulas pero si un gran pico plano más grande que el de Iguanodon

facts.statement: The skull structure provided a larger insertion area for jaw muscles, allowing for a stronger bite.
facts.quote: Esto le proveyó una mayor área del inserción para los músculos de la quijada, permitiéndole una mordedura más fuerte.

facts.statement: Bumps distributed from the nasal opening to the top of the skull were likely used for social displays or mating rituals, though their exact significance is unknown.
facts.quote: Había un número de topetones que se distribuían desde la abertura nasal al techo del cráneo, su significación es desconocido, pero pudieron haber sido utilizados para las exhibiciones durante la socialización o el celo.

facts.statement: The premaxillae measured 46.0 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: Los premaxilares miden 46,0 centímetros de largo

facts.statement: Only the right maxilla is known, well-preserved as a triangle 28.0 centimeters long and 11.7 centimeters high.
facts.quote: Solo el maxilar derecho de Ouranosaurus es conocida. aunque está bien conservado formando un triángulo de 28,0 centímetros de largo y 11,7 centímetros de alto

facts.statement: The axial column consisted of eleven cervical vertebrae, seventeen dorsal vertebrae, six sacral vertebrae, and forty caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: La columna axial constaba de once vértebras del cuello, diecisiete vértebras dorsales, seis vértebras sacras y cuarenta vértebras de la cola.

facts.statement: The most conspicuous feature of Ouranosaurus was a large sail on its back, supported by long and wide neural spines extending over its rump and tail.
facts.quote: La característica más conspicua de Ouranosaurus es una gran "vela" en su espalda, sostenida por espinas neurales largas y anchas, que abarca toda su rabadilla y cola

facts.statement: The tenth, eleventh, and twelfth spines were the longest, measuring about 63 centimeters.
facts.quote: Las espinas décima, undécima y duodécima son las más largas, con unos 63 centímetros.

facts.statement: An alternative hypothesis suggests the back might have had a hump of muscle or fat, similar to a bison or camel, rather than a sail.
facts.quote: Una hipótesis alternativa es que la espalda podría haber tenido una joroba compuesta de tejido muscular o grasa, parecida a la de un bisonte o un camello, en lugar de una vela.

facts.statement: The forelimbs were quite long, reaching 55% of the length of the hindlimbs.
facts.quote: Las extremidades anteriores eran bastante largas con el 55% de la longitud de las extremidades posteriores.

facts.statement: Each hand possessed a thumb spur claw that was much smaller than that of Iguanodon.
facts.quote: En cada mano Ouranosaurus poseía una garra del pulgar en forma de espolón, que era mucho más pequeño que el de Iguanodon.

facts.statement: The second and third fingers were broad and hoof-like, anatomically suited for walking.
facts.quote: Los dedos segundo y tercero eran anchos y parecían cascos , y anatómicamente eran buenos para caminar.

facts.statement: Large muscular cheeks would have prevented food, leaves, fruits, and seeds from falling out of the mouth.
facts.quote: Grandes mejillas musculares habrían evitado que la comida, hojas, frutas y semillas se le cayeran de la boca.

facts.statement: Spaces between tooth crowns were filled with the tips of a second generation of replacement teeth, forming a continuous surface.
facts.quote: los espacios entre las coronas de los dientes se rellenaron con las puntas de una segunda generación de dientes de reemplazo, todo formando una superficie continua.

facts.statement: The dorsal sail is usually explained as a thermoregulation system or a display structure.
facts.quote: La "vela" dorsal se suele explicar como un sistema de termorregulación o una estructura de visualización.

facts.statement: The back structure could have been used for energy storage to survive periods of scarcity.
facts.quote: Podría haberse utilizado para el almacenamiento de energía para sobrevivir a una temporada de escasez.

facts.statement: A quadrupedal posture would have been possible.
facts.quote: Habría sido posible una postura cuadrúpeda.

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus had long, solid hind legs designed to support its body weight.
facts.quote: Sus miembros posteriores eran largos y sólidos para soportar el peso del cuerpo.

facts.statement: The femur of Ouranosaurus was as long as the tibia, and its foot was small with three toes.
facts.quote: El fémur era tan largo como la tibia, y el pie era pequeño con tres dedos.

facts.statement: The femur of Ouranosaurus was slightly longer than the tibia.
facts.quote: El fémur era un poco más largo que la tibia.

facts.statement: The foot of Ouranosaurus was narrow, relatively long, and had only three toes.
facts.quote: El pie era estrecho con solo tres dedos y relativamente largo.

facts.statement: The prepubis in the pelvis of Ouranosaurus was very large, rounded, and directed obliquely upward.
facts.quote: En la pelvis, el prepubis era muy grande, redondeado y dirigido oblicuamente hacia arriba.

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus is often depicted with a large skin sail on its back supported by long dorsal spines running along its back and part of its tail, similar to Spinosaurus and Dimetrodon.
facts.quote: Al igual que en Spinosaurus, un terópodo de aproximadamente la misma época y lugar, y el Dimetrodon del Pérmico, Ouranosaurus se lo suele representar con una gran "vela" de piel en su espalda, soportada por largas espinas dorsales, que recorrían toda su espalda y parte de la cola.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the dorsal spines of Ouranosaurus may have supported a hump rather than a sail, similar to a bison or camel.
facts.quote: Todas estas características indican que el dinosaurio pudo haber tenido una joroba, similar a las del bisonte o camello más que una vela.

facts.statement: The proposed hump on Ouranosaurus might have served as a fat reserve during times of scarcity.
facts.quote: Esta habría podido ser utilizado como fuente de reservas durante las épocas de escasez.

facts.statement: The dorsal spines of Ouranosaurus were connected by tendons that tightened the posterior part of the back.
facts.quote: Las espinas dorsales también estaban unidas por los tendones, que atiesaron la parte posterior de la espalda.

facts.statement: The dorsal spines of Ouranosaurus were tallest above the front legs.
facts.quote: Finalmente, la longitud de la espina dorsal es más alta sobre los miembros anteriores.

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus had only small temporal openings behind its eyes where the large capiti-mandibularis muscle attached to the coronoid process of the lower jaw bone.
facts.quote: Ouranosaurus tenía solo pequeñas aberturas temporales detrás de los ojos, desde las cuales se unía el músculo capiti-mandibularis más grande a la apófisis coronoides en el hueso de la mandíbula inferior.

facts.statement: Small rounded horns in front of its eyes made Ouranosaurus the only known horned ornithopod.
facts.quote: Los pequeños cuernos redondeados frente a sus ojos hicieron de Ouranosaurus el único ornitópodo cornudo conocido.

facts.statement: The narrow back of the skull of Ouranosaurus could not compensate for the lack of a larger area for jaw muscle attachment, resulting in less bite power.
facts.quote: La parte posterior del cráneo era bastante estrecha y no podía compensar la falta de un área mayor de unión para el músculo de la mandíbula, que normalmente proporcionarían las aberturas, lo que permite más potencia y una mordida más fuerte.

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus likely used its teeth to chew on hard plant foods.
facts.quote: Ouranosaurus probablemente usó sus dientes para masticar alimentos vegetales duros.

facts.statement: A diet of leaves, fruits, and seeds has been suggested for Ouranosaurus, with its wide beak indicating specialization for consuming large quantities of low-quality forage.
facts.quote: Se ha sugerido una dieta de hojas, frutos y semillas, ya que masticar permitiría liberar más energía de alimentos de alta calidad, el pico ancho por otro lado indica una especialización en comer grandes cantidades de forraje de baja calidad.

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus lived from the Aptian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 121.4 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Maastrichtian (121.4 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 8 recorded fossil occurrences of Ouranosaurus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 8

facts.statement: The parent group of Ouranosaurus is Neoiguanodontia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Neoiguanodontia

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus is placed within the clade Hadrosauroidea, which contains true hadrosaurids, the "duck-billed dinosaurs" that were abundant in the late Cretaceous, and their close relatives.

facts.statement: Ouranosaurus appears to represent an early specialized branch in the Hadrosauroidea group, showing some independent convergence with hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: Ouranosaurus parece representar una rama especializada temprana en este grupo, mostrando en algunos rasgos una convergencia independiente con los hadrosáuridos.

facts.statement: Therefore, Ouranosaurus is considered a basal hadrosauriform.
facts.quote: Por tanto, es un hadrosauriforme basal.
